logs.title: Log collection
logs.intro: OPNexus regularly fetches firewall logs from all hosts and stores them in its own database (see “Logs”). Longer retention means more storage, depending on the traffic volume of the connected firewalls — on heavily used hosts, even a few days can take up several gigabytes.
logs.maxSizeHint: 0 = unlimited. When the limit is reached the oldest entries are deleted. The value is estimated from the table size; Postgres does not hand freed space back to the file system but reuses it for new logs.

update.title: Update OPNexus
update.hint: Pulls the new images, switches the services and checks that everything is healthy. If that fails, OPNexus rolls back to the previous version automatically.
update.feedOff: The version check is off. Set UPDATE_CHECK_URL in the server's .env so OPNexus can detect new versions.
update.feedError: The release feed is currently unreachable.
update.notEnabledTitle: Updates from the web interface are not enabled.
update.notEnabledBody: They need a small separate service (the updater) with access to Docker — deliberately optional. To enable it:
update.notEnabledStep1: Add to the .env on the server:
update.notEnabledCli: Until then, update on the server with “opnexus update”.
update.unreachable: The updater does not respond. Check on the server: docker compose ps updater
update.localMode: This installation builds OPNexus locally from source (no release image). Update on the server with git pull and docker compose up -d --build.
update.majorChange: Version {latest} is a major version jump. Please read the release notes first, then update on the server with “opnexus update {latest}”.
update.confirmBody: OPNexus pulls the new images and restarts itself. The interface is unavailable for about one to two minutes; the managed firewalls are not affected.
update.confirmSafety: A backup is taken automatically before a database migration. If the new version does not become healthy, OPNexus rolls back to the previous version on its own.
update.reconnecting: Reconnecting — this is normal while the services restart.

result.succeededUpdate: OPNexus is now running {version}. Reloading the page …
result.succeededRollback: OPNexus was rolled back to {version}. Reloading the page …
result.rolledBack: The update to {target} failed. OPNexus was rolled back to the previous version automatically.
result.failed: The operation failed. Check the log and the server state (on the server: opnexus status).

rollback.dataLoss: The update migrated the database. Rolling back restores the state from before the update: changes made since the update and the log history are lost.
rollback.noDataLoss: The database was not migrated — no data is lost.

maint.cancelWarnPost: a successful completion — it only closes the record so the host/cluster is no longer locked. Use this only if the expected state demonstrably never occurred (e.g. a CARP role switch is stuck).
maint.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. CARP role switch did not happen after several minutes
maint.unattendedWarning: Runs unattended at the chosen time. For updates, OPNexus takes a configuration backup itself right before. The other prerequisites are only re-checked then — if one is not met, the action is not executed and is marked as failed, without a retry.

maint.handoverOption: Switch to the partner first and switch back afterwards (CARP)
maint.handoverHint: Flow: maintenance mode on this host, the partner becomes MASTER (verified), then the action runs, and once the host is back the maintenance mode is left again. If anything goes wrong the partner stays MASTER and a notification is sent. When switching back, the host may take the MASTER role back depending on the CARP settings (a short second switchover).

groups.emptyText: For example, create “Sites” or “Data center” and pick the matching firewalls.
groups.onlyHosts: So far the group only bundles hosts. Assign a central rule to it now.
groups.descPlaceholder: Shared base rules for all sites
groups.membershipNote: Memberships take effect at the next push. Saving does not change any firewall. Rules that are already deployed remain on removed members.
groups.impactEmpty: No rules or aliases are assigned to the group yet. The change only affects its members and description.
groups.newRuleTargets: {added} new rule targets · {removed} removed rule targets
groups.retainedCopies: {count} already deployed copies remain. After saving, clean them up selectively under “Review & push”.
groups.natRetained: {count} deployed copies remain. Clean them up selectively under NAT.
groups.otherGroupNote: Hosts that remain a target of the same rule through another group or directly are not counted as removed rule targets.

aliases.deleteConfirm: Really delete this alias? It will also be removed from all target hosts.
aliases.title: Firewall aliases
aliases.subtitle: Centrally managed objects (hosts, networks, ports) — maintain once, deploy to several firewalls instead of keeping each one in sync individually.
aliases.hierarchyHint: The alias is additionally deployed to all current and future hosts in the subtree.

hint.host: One IP or host name per line
hint.port: One port number or range per line, e.g. 8080 or 8000:8100
hint.networkgroup: One alias name per line (combines other aliases)
hint.mac: One MAC address per line, e.g. 00:11:22:33:44:55
hint.asn: One AS number per line, e.g. 64512

ph.deleteRuleConfirm: Really delete rule “{name}”? It will also be removed from all target hosts.
ph.orderSaved: Order saved. Apply it to already deployed rules with “Re-establish order”.
ph.reassertDone: Order for “{name}” and all subgroups has been re-established.
ph.title: Hierarchical policies
ph.subtitle: Define pre/post rules on parent groups — they are deployed automatically, in the correct order, to all hosts of the group and its subgroups.
ph.selectGroupHint: Rules are defined on a group and automatically reach all hosts of that group and its subgroups.
ph.reassertTitle: Applies the saved order on all hosts of this group and its subgroups. It is also checked automatically after other OPNexus deployments.
ph.preHint: Evaluated before the post rules. Across several levels: root-most group first.
ph.postHint: Evaluated after the pre rules. Across several levels: leaf-most (most specific) group first.
ph.noRulesInCategory: No rules in this category yet.

certs.certDeleteConfirm: Really delete certificate “{name}”? If it was already pushed to the firewall, it is removed there as well (unless in use).
certs.title: Certificates
certs.subtitle: Live fleet overview as well as central management of trust store certificates and ACME/Let's Encrypt issuance.
certs.attentionOne: {count} certificate expires within the next 30 days or has already expired.
certs.attentionMany: {count} certificates expire within the next 30 days or have already expired.
certs.trustIntro: OPNsense core trust store (import/create internally/CSR/CA-sign/manual) — managed per host, since internal CA references and certificate UUIDs are host-local. A push is a single, immediately effective API call without a service restart — no warning needed, as there is no lockout risk.
certs.createHostFirst: Create at least one host first.
certs.acmeIntro: ACME plugin (os-acme-client) — accounts and certificate requests managed per host (host-local UUIDs). Creating/changing is a purely local configuration change; “Register” and “Issue now” contact the real certificate authority and are therefore hidden behind an explicit warning.
certs.createAccountFirst: Create at least one ACME account first.
certs.requestMeta: {host} · Account: {account} · Renewal every {days} days (since last issuance)

ipsec.pskRequired: A pre-shared key is required when creating a tunnel
ipsec.deleteConfirm: Really delete this tunnel? It will also be removed from all target hosts (connection, identities, phase 2, pre-shared key) and the IPsec service will be reloaded.
ipsec.title: IPsec VPN (site-to-site)
ipsec.intro: Site-to-site tunnels with pre-shared-key authentication, maintained centrally and deployed to target hosts or device groups — analogous to the firewall rules, but without their automatic rollback safety net: a failed service reload can cut exactly the connection OPNexus uses to reach the host. v1 only supports PSK auth, one phase 2 (child) per tunnel and simple 1:1 network-to-network tunnels — no OpenVPN/WireGuard, no certificates/EAP, no pools.
ipsec.pskSet: set — leave empty to keep it

ovpn.deleteConfirm: Really delete this OpenVPN instance? It will also be removed from all target hosts (instance, static key if any) and the OpenVPN service will be reloaded.
ovpn.title: OpenVPN instances
ovpn.intro: OpenVPN instances (server or client role), maintained centrally and deployed to target hosts or device groups — analogous to the IPsec feature, but without its automatic rollback safety net: a failed service reload can cut exactly the connection OPNexus uses to reach the host. v1 requires a certificate/CA that already exists on every target host — selectable via a picker from the respective host's trust store, since a certificate UUID is host-local —, supports optional TLS hardening (tls-auth/tls-crypt) via a static key, but no certificate-less “shared key” instance (not provided for in the modern OPNsense model).
ovpn.tlsKeyMissing: TLS key enabled but not stored
ovpn.tlsHardeningLabel: TLS hardening (tls-auth/tls-crypt) via an additional static key
ovpn.noTargets: No target hosts selected — select hosts or a device group above; the selection then appears here, per host from its own trust store.
ovpn.noCerts: No certificates found on this host.
ovpn.noCas: No CAs found on this host.

wg.deleteConfirm: Really delete this WireGuard tunnel? It will also be removed from all target hosts (peer, then server) and the WireGuard service will be reloaded.
wg.title: WireGuard tunnels
wg.intro: WireGuard interconnects (one server interface + exactly one peer per tunnel), maintained centrally and deployed to target hosts or device groups — analogous to IPsec/OpenVPN, without their automatic rollback safety net: a failed service reload can cut exactly the connection OPNexus uses to reach the host. v1 requires the server private key AND public key as well as the peer public key to be supplied manually by the operator (no key pair generator), optionally supports WireGuard's own pre-shared key per peer, and models exactly one server↔peer connection (no multi-peer hub).
wg.keyNote: OPNexus does not generate key pairs (no automatic call to OPNsense's own “gen_keypair”). Generate both keys yourself (e.g. via {cmd}) and enter them here.
wg.endpointPort: Endpoint port (required if an address is set)
wg.pskLabel: Additional pre-shared key for this peer (WireGuard's own PSK, not IPsec's PSK)

auditExport.title: Audit export
auditExport.intro: Forwards the audit trail (who changed what, with status) to a syslog server and/or a webhook, so it also exists outside OPNexus. Only new events are sent from the moment you switch it on; firewall object contents are never included. Delivery is at least once: every event carries its id.
auditExport.testFailed: The test message could not be delivered

backupSettings.title: Backups
backupSettings.intro: Takes a configuration backup of every firewall on a schedule and keeps the newest ones. Optionally a copy is encrypted here with your passphrase and uploaded to S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Cloudflare R2, Hetzner…), so a lost OPNexus server or a lost firewall is not the end of your configuration. Delete old offsite copies with the bucket's lifecycle rules.
backupSettings.scheduled: Back up all firewalls on a schedule
backupSettings.pathStyle: Path-style addressing (works everywhere; turn off only if your provider needs bucket.host)
backupSettings.passphraseHint: Backups are encrypted before they leave this server. Without the passphrase an offsite copy cannot be read — keep it somewhere safe besides OPNexus. Changing it only affects new uploads.
backupSettings.testOk: The target works (written, read back, deleted)

backupDiff.title: Changes since the previous backup
backupDiff.hint: Secrets (passwords, keys, tokens, certificates) are shown as hashes only: a changed secret appears as a changed hash.
backupDiff.truncated: The list is cut off; compare the files in OPNsense for the rest.

overlay.title: Management tunnel
overlay.intro: Lets OPNexus manage firewalls that have no public address (behind NAT, CGNAT, a mobile link). Each firewall dials OUT to a WireGuard hub on this server; OPNexus then reaches its API through the tunnel. Nothing on the firewall has to be reachable from the internet. Needs the hub container (COMPOSE_PROFILES=overlay) and the UDP port reachable from the internet.
overlay.loadFailed: Could not load the management tunnel
overlay.hubAbsent: The hub container is not running. Add COMPOSE_PROFILES=overlay to .env and run docker compose up -d.
overlay.endpoint: Address of this server (as the firewalls see it)
overlay.endpointHint: Public DNS name or IP of this server. Add :port if the published UDP port differs.
overlay.subnetHint: A private network used only for these tunnels. Cannot be changed while firewalls are registered.
overlay.nameHint: A name for this firewall or site.
overlay.deleteConfirm: Remove “{name}” from the management tunnel? The firewall will no longer be reachable through it.
overlay.howIntro: Do this once in the firewall's own web interface (OPNsense: VPN › WireGuard). Copy the values with the buttons.
overlay.step1Hint: Create a new instance: let OPNsense generate its key pair, no listen port is needed, and enter this tunnel address:
overlay.step3Text: Add a firewall rule on the WireGuard interface group: pass TCP from {hub} to “This Firewall”, port 443 (or the port of the web interface).
overlay.step4: 4. Give OPNexus the firewall's public key
overlay.step4Text: Copy the public key of the new local instance from OPNsense, close this window and use “Key / host” on this firewall.
overlay.step5: 5. Add the firewall as a host
overlay.step5Text: Add or edit the host with this address and the usual API key. It then shows up as connected here.
overlay.firewallKey: Public key of the firewall's WireGuard instance
overlay.firewallKeyHint: From OPNsense: VPN › WireGuard › Instances. Leave empty to remove it.
overlay.hostHint: Optional: which managed host is reached through this tunnel.

variables.title: Site variables
variables.intro: Rules, aliases and NAT entries can contain placeholders like {{LAN_NET}}. Each firewall fills them with its own value, so one object serves many sites with different networks. A firewall without a value for a placeholder is never pushed: the preview says so and the deploy is refused. Values may contain letters, digits and . : / , @ + - _ and spaces.
variables.empty: No placeholders in use. Write {{NAME}} into a rule, alias or NAT entry (capital letters, digits and _) and define its value here.

sso.title: Single sign-on (OIDC)
sso.intro: Lets people sign in with your identity provider (Authentik, Keycloak, Entra ID, Google, …) instead of a password stored here. Roles come from the provider's groups at every login; without a mapped group nobody gets in. Local accounts keep working, so you can always sign in with the admin password if the provider is down.
sso.testOk: The provider answered (discovery and signing keys are fine)
sso.enable: Offer single sign-on on the login page
sso.redirectHint: Register this redirect URI with your provider:
sso.name: Button text
sso.mappingHint: Enter the group names as the provider sends them. The most privileged matching role wins; a person in none of them cannot sign in. Roles of SSO accounts are managed at the provider and refreshed at every login. Providers that only send groups when asked (e.g. Okta) need the scope "groups" added to the scopes.
sso.dutiesIntro: When switched off, operators can prepare changes (edit, preview) but only an administrator may roll them out: deploy, remove or roll back a deployment, run or schedule maintenance and apply network changes. The refusal is recorded in the audit.
sso.operatorsDeploy: Operators may roll out changes themselves

security.title: Security posture
security.intro: Checks every firewall's configuration for common weaknesses (open rules, weak SSH/SNMP, missing backups…) and gives a score from 0 to 100. Read-only: nothing is changed on the firewalls. Checked automatically every 6 hours.
security.loadFailed: Could not load the security posture
security.noHostsHint: Connect a firewall to see its security posture.

errorHint.unreachable: The firewall could not be reached, so it could not be checked.
errorHint.invalid_config: The configuration could not be read.

reason.root_password: root may log in over SSH with a password

webgui_https.title: Web interface over HTTPS only
webgui_https.ok: The management interface is served over HTTPS.
webgui_https.fail: The management interface runs over unencrypted HTTP. Credentials can be read on the network.
webgui_https.fix: System › Settings › Administration: set the protocol to HTTPS.

ssh_hardened.title: SSH locked down
ssh_hardened.ok: SSH is off or accepts keys only.
ssh_hardened.fix: Switch SSH off, or disable root login and password login under System › Settings › Administration and use keys.

snmp_community.title: SNMP community is not “public”
snmp_community.fail: SNMP uses the default community “public”. Anyone on the network can read system data.
snmp_community.fix: Set your own long community or turn SNMP off.

wan_any_any.title: No allow-all rule on the WAN
wan_any_any.ok: No rule on the WAN allows all traffic to everywhere.
wan_any_any.fail: {count} rule(s) on the WAN allow all traffic to any destination — the firewall protects nothing there.
wan_any_any.fix: Restrict the rule to the sources, destinations and ports you need, or delete it.

internal_any_any.title: No allow-all rule from any source (internal)
internal_any_any.ok: No internal rule allows any source to any destination.
internal_any_any.fail: {count} rule(s) allow any source to any destination.
internal_any_any.fix: Limit the source to the network the rule is meant for.

rules_shadowed.title: No shadowed rules
rules_shadowed.fail: {count} rule(s) are never reached because an earlier rule already covers them.
rules_shadowed.fix: Check the order; remove the useless rule or move it up.

rules_duplicate.title: No duplicate rules
rules_duplicate.fail: {count} rule(s) are identical to an earlier one.

rules_documented.title: Rules are described
rules_documented.ok: All active rules have a description.
rules_documented.fix: Add a description so it stays clear later what the rule is for.

ntp_configured.title: Time server set
ntp_configured.fail: No time server is configured. Logs and certificates need the right time.
ntp_configured.fix: Enter NTP servers in the time settings.

remote_logging.title: Logs are kept elsewhere too
remote_logging.ok: A remote syslog target is configured.
remote_logging.fail: Logs exist only on the firewall. After a break-in or a failure they are gone.
remote_logging.fix: Add a syslog server under System › Settings › Logging.

ids_enabled.title: Intrusion detection active
ids_enabled.fail: Intrusion detection (IDS/IPS) is not switched on.

firmware_current.title: Firmware up to date
firmware_current.fix: Install them in the Update Center.
firmware_current.unknown: Could not determine the update status.

backup_recent.title: Recent backup
backup_recent.ok: The newest backup is {days} day(s) old.
backup_recent.fail: There is no backup from the last 7 days.
backup_recent.fix: Use “Back up now” on the host page or schedule maintenance.

rules_unused.title: Rules in use
rules_unused.ok: Every rule matched traffic in the last 30 days.
rules_unused.fail: {count} rule(s) have matched nothing for at least 30 days.
rules_unused.unknown: Still collecting data: a rule counts as unused only after 30 days without a hit.
rules_unused.fix: Check whether the rule is still needed and disable or delete it.

hits.title: Rule usage
hits.intro: When each rule last matched traffic, as observed by OPNexus. The firewall's own counters restart with every change and reboot, so OPNexus keeps the last time it saw one grow. A rule counts as unused after 30 days without a hit.

tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: Tokens let scripts, CI jobs, Prometheus and AI assistants use the OPNexus API without a sign-in. Each token belongs to you, has a scope and can be revoked at any time. It never gets more rights than your account.
tokens.nameHint: What the token is for, e.g. “Grafana” or “CI deploy”.

scopeHint.read: Read only: view everything, change nothing. For dashboards, Prometheus and AI assistants.
scopeHint.deploy: Read plus roll out rules, aliases, NAT, VPN and maintenance. Cannot manage users, settings or hosts.
scopeHint.admin: Everything your account may do, except managing tokens and your own account.

tokens.passwordHint: Creating a token needs your current password.
tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke token “{name}”? Anything using it stops working immediately.
tokens.shownOnce: Copy the token now. It is shown only once and cannot be displayed again.

users.ssoTip: Managed by single sign-on: role and password are changed at the identity provider.
users.title: Users
users.intro: “Admin” may do everything. “Operator” rolls out and operates (rules, NAT, VPN, maintenance) but cannot manage users, settings or hosts. “Read-only” can view all pages and data but cannot save changes — only your own password can always be changed.
users.cannotDeleteSelf: You cannot delete your own account

logs.title: Firewall logs
logs.noBlocked: No blocked connections in this period.
logs.noEntries: No log entries for this selection.

cluster.ungroupedHint: These hosts have no cluster name — assign one under Hosts ▸ Edit to see them grouped here.

about.tagline: Central management of multiple OPNsense firewalls.

audit.title: Deploy audit history
audit.intro: Requests and deployment results are stored permanently from activation onwards, even after a rule or host is deleted. “Request processed” describes the HTTP request; the separate host entry shows the deploy result. Earlier actions are not reconstructed retroactively.

hostDetail.noManagedRules: No centrally managed rules for this host.
hostDetail.liveRulesTitle: Actually configured rules (live from the firewall)
hostDetail.noManagedAliases: No centrally managed aliases for this host.
hostDetail.liveAliasesTitle: Actually configured aliases (live from the firewall)

haOrder.title: HA order
haOrder.master: This node is currently MASTER. Update the BACKUP node first. Then switch the CARP roles in OPNsense and return to this node.
haOrder.backup: In an HA cluster, updates are only started on the current BACKUP node.

partner.title: HA partner not ready
partner.text: The other cluster node must be online and CARP MASTER before this node can be updated.

backup.title: Fresh backup required
backup.text: Before installing, OPNexus needs a local configuration backup that is at most 24 hours old.

noUpdate.title: No installable update
noUpdate.text: The last check reports no stable package update.

noMajor.title: No installable major upgrade
noMajor.text: The last check reports no available major upgrade.

pending.title: Maintenance still open
pending.text: An earlier maintenance must be completed first, after the technical check.

change.title: Change still open
change.text: A deployment or rollback in the cluster is not finished yet.

updates.autoRunning: Automatic update check running on {count} hosts…
updates.backupSaved: Fresh configuration backup for {host} was saved.
updates.outcomeUnclear: Outcome unclear. Check the maintenance status.
updates.cancelledNote: Operation on {host} was closed without confirmed completion.
updates.title: Update Center
updates.intro: When opened, all eligible hosts are automatically checked for updates. Major upgrades and HA role switches remain deliberate manual steps.
updates.readOnlyNote: Read-only access: status, package changes and logs are visible; checks and updates are blocked.
updates.whyMajorBlocked: Why “Prepare major upgrade” is still blocked
updates.noPackageChanges: No stable package changes in the cached check result.
updates.majorWarnTitle: Major upgrade: switch to a new major version
updates.majorWarnText: Takes longer and is riskier than a plain package update, possibly with larger behaviour changes to services and configuration. Have a fresh backup and console access ready before proceeding.
updates.plannedDowntimeText: The host may be unreachable during installation. Connections may drop; there is no automatic rollback.
updates.finishCheckCarp: Check the CARP roles and reachability of both cluster nodes.
updates.finishCheck: Check reachability, installed version and services.
updates.finishNote: This confirmation documents the check and does not trigger any further firewall action.
updates.cancelWarnPost: a successful completion — it only closes the record so this host/cluster is no longer locked. Only use it if the expected state demonstrably never occurred (e.g. a CARP role switch is stuck).
updates.logEmpty: No log available. OPNsense clears it on reboot – after a successful update that is normal. The firewall's status shown on this page is what counts.
updates.tipCheckAll: Asks all eligible firewalls for new updates. Nothing is installed.
updates.tipRefreshView: Reloads the last known status of all hosts without contacting the firewalls.
updates.tipCheck: Asks this firewall for available updates. Nothing is installed.
updates.tipPrepare: Shows a preview first. Nothing is installed until you explicitly confirm.
updates.tipPrepareMajor: Switch to a new major version: takes longer and is riskier. A preview comes first.
updates.tipFinish: Check the result on the firewall and document the completion.
updates.tipCancel: Closes a stuck operation without confirming success. Only if the expected state never occurred.
updates.tipPackages: Packages that will change with the next update
updates.tipLog: Shows the log of the last update action on the firewall
updates.tipBackup: A local configuration backup no older than 24 hours is required before any update.
updates.tipInstalled: Version currently installed on the firewall
updates.tipAvailable: Newest version that can be installed according to the last check
updates.tipRebootRequired: The firewall must be rebooted after the update and will be briefly unreachable.
updates.majorWarnShort: Switch to a new major version
updates.majorWarnTip: Takes longer and is riskier than a package update, possibly with behavior changes to services and configuration. Have a fresh backup and console access ready.
updates.downtimeShort: The host may be unreachable during installation
updates.downtimeTip: Connections can drop. There is no automatic rollback.
updates.tipConfirmName: Typing the host name prevents updating the wrong host by accident.
updates.confirmRunDisabledName: Enter the host name exactly to continue
updates.cancelWarnShort: Does not confirm a successful completion
updates.cancelWarnTip: The operation is only closed so the host or cluster does not stay locked. Use only if the expected state demonstrably never occurred (e.g. a stuck CARP role switch).
updates.finishNoteTip: This confirmation documents your check and triggers no firewall action.

tls.title: Firewall TLS certificate
tls.intro: The connection to the firewall is only accepted as secure if it presents exactly this certificate. This works for IP addresses and names alike and protects against eavesdropping and redirection.
tls.subject: Name
tls.confirmMatch: The fingerprint matches the firewall's certificate.
tls.confirmHelp: Compare it in OPNsense under System → Trust → Certificates (web GUI certificate) or in the browser's certificate dialog for the firewall. Only confirm if it matches exactly.
tls.skipVerifyHelp: The connection stays encrypted, but OPNexus cannot tell whether the firewall is really answering. For testing only.
tls.probeFailed: The certificate could not be retrieved
tls.systemTip: Standard certificate check. For self-signed firewalls, pin the certificate.
tls.insecureTip: The certificate is not verified. Edit the host to pin it.

twofa.title: Two-factor sign-in
twofa.intro: In addition to the password, sign-in asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (e.g. Aegis, Google Authenticator, 1Password). Protects the account even if the password becomes known.
twofa.confirmPasswordHelp: The password is asked again so that a stolen session alone cannot register someone else's authenticator.
twofa.scan: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, then enter the code it shows.
twofa.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app
twofa.codesHelp: Each code works exactly once if you lose your device. They are only shown now.
twofa.savedAck: I have saved the codes in a safe place.
twofa.enterCodeOrRecovery: Code from the app or recovery code
twofa.resetTip: Removes this user's two-factor sign-in, e.g. when the device was lost.

network.managementNote: OPNexus reaches this firewall through {device}. Changes to this interface can cut the connection and will get extra safeguards later.
network.managementUnknown: Which interface OPNexus uses to reach this firewall cannot be determined (e.g. via NAT or a CARP address).
network.cannotConfigure: This firewall is too old to change interface IPs through its API (possible from OPNsense 26.7.6). Change the IP directly in OPNsense or update the firewall.

risks.management_interface: This change affects {device}, the interface OPNexus uses to reach the firewall. The connection may drop.
risks.management_address: The address {address} is the one OPNexus uses to reach the firewall.
risks.management_unknown: Which interface OPNexus uses to reach this firewall cannot be determined (NAT or a CARP address). The impact cannot be judged.
risks.default_gateway: {name} is the default gateway. Without it, traffic to the internet may fail.
risks.default_gateway_change: The default gateway is being set or switched. All outbound traffic will take a different path afterwards.
risks.management_gateway: {name} sits on the interface OPNexus uses to reach the firewall.
risks.default_route: A default route ({network}) changes the path for almost all traffic.
risks.route_covers_management: The route {network} covers the firewall's own address. Replies to OPNexus may take a different path.
risks.interface_rules_removed: Removing it makes OPNsense itself delete {count} rule(s) that use this interface: {names}
risks.management_member: {device} is the interface OPNexus uses to reach the firewall, and it is a member of this device. The connection may drop.
risks.tunable_change: Tunables change how the whole system behaves; some only apply after a reboot and some can make the firewall unusable.

warnings.carp_change: CARP changes can trigger a switch between master and backup.
warnings.cluster_peers: This firewall is part of a cluster. The same change may be needed on {hosts} as well. VIPs and gateways are not synchronised automatically.
warnings.core_interface: {name} is a core interface of the firewall. Changes affect every rule and service on it.
warnings.gateway_group_in_use: Rules that use this gateway group lose their target.

blocks.api_unavailable: This firewall does not offer an API for this ({section}).
blocks.interface_api_unavailable: This firewall is too old to configure interfaces through its API (possible from OPNsense 26.7.6). Please change it directly in OPNsense or update the firewall.
blocks.interface_changes_pending: Interface changes are already staged on the firewall and waiting to be applied. Check and apply or discard them there first.
blocks.interface_locked: The interface is locked. Remove the lock first, then delete.
blocks.tunable_default_row: This is a built-in default of the firewall. To change it, create your own entry with “Override”.

change.loadFailed: The form could not be loaded.
change.previewFailed: The preview could not be created.
change.applyFailed: The change could not be applied.
change.riskTitle: Careful, this change can cut the connection
change.backupNote: A backup of the firewall configuration is saved before applying. There is no automatic rollback: if the connection drops, OPNexus cannot undo the change itself.
change.ack: I understand that this change can cut the connection to {host} and is not rolled back automatically.
change.typeHost: To confirm, type the firewall's name: {host}
change.unreachable: The change was applied, but “{host}” no longer answers on its previous address. If the management address was changed, enter the new one under Hosts › Edit. The backup taken before the change is kept.
change.transferHint: Apply the same change to the partner in the cluster as well? Backup node first, then the master.

hint.interfaceDescr: Letters, digits and underscores only (no spaces or hyphens).

network.objectsUnavailable: This OPNsense version offers no API for this.

compare.noClusters: No cluster with at least two hosts.
compare.intro: Compares the network configuration of a cluster's nodes. Addresses, CARP advskew and the active default gateway may differ and are not compared.

intro.tunables: System parameters of the firewall (sysctl). The firewall's own values stay untouched; your own entries override them.
intro.cron: Scheduled tasks the firewall runs itself.
intro.syslog: Remote log targets the firewall sends its messages to.
intro.snapshots: ZFS snapshots of the firewall as an extra safety net before bigger changes. Activating one (with a reboot) is deliberately left to OPNsense itself.
intro.diagnostics: Network queries the selected firewall runs itself (reachability, paths, ports, name resolution). Results are only shown; every run is recorded with its target in the audit log.

snapshots.createHint: The snapshot captures the current system state. It does not replace a configuration backup.
snapshots.name: Name
snapshots.nameHint: Letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen.
snapshots.unsupported: This firewall does not support snapshots (no ZFS).

diag.name: Name
diag.sourceHint: The firewall's own address to query from. Empty = automatic.

setup.title: Setup assistant
setup.readOnly: The assistant sets up the account and firewalls, so it is reserved for administrators.

welcome.title: Welcome to OPNexus
welcome.intro: OPNexus manages your OPNsense firewalls in one place: rules, NAT, VPN, certificates, updates and HA clusters. This assistant sets up the essentials in a few minutes. You can skip it at any time and reopen it later under System › Setup.

points.account: Secure the account: your own password and two-factor sign-in.
points.firewall: Connect your first firewall: create an API key, check the certificate, done.
points.done: An overview of what makes sense next.

welcome.readOnlyNote: The assistant only reads from your firewall. Nothing there changes until you roll something out yourself later.

account.title: Secure the account
account.passwordIntro: If you did not set ADMIN_PASSWORD at startup, OPNexus generated a random password. Set your own now. This step is optional.
account.currentHint: The password you just signed in with. Lost it? On the server: ./opnexus password
account.newHint: At least 10 characters. A password manager is the most convenient way.
account.twofaIntro: OPNexus can change firewalls. A second factor from an authenticator app protects the account even if the password becomes known.

firewall.title: Connect your first firewall
firewall.intro: OPNexus talks to your OPNsense through its REST API, which needs an API key. Creating one takes a minute.
firewall.offlineHelp: Check the address and API key, and that the firewall allows web interface access from this server.
firewall.keyTitle: How to create the API key in OPNsense

keySteps.menu: In OPNsense open System › Access › Users.
keySteps.user: Create a dedicated user (e.g. “opnexus”) or edit an existing one.
keySteps.key: Under “API keys” on that user click the plus. Your browser downloads a file called apikey.txt.
keySteps.rights: Give the user sufficient privileges, most simply the “admin” group. With fewer privileges individual features fail.

firewall.keyFileNote: In apikey.txt the key follows key= and the secret follows secret=. The secret exists only in this file.
firewall.nameHint: Free choice, display only. For an HA pair e.g. fw-a and fw-b.
firewall.urlHint: Address of the OPNsense web interface, with https:// and the port if needed, e.g. https://192.168.1.1:8443.
firewall.clusterHint: Is the firewall an HA pair? Add both nodes as separate firewalls and give both the same cluster name.
firewall.connectNote: OPNexus checks right away whether the firewall answers.

done.title: Done

rules.title: Create rules
rules.text: New rules are rolled out with a confirmation: if you do not confirm within {seconds} seconds, OPNexus rolls back automatically.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.text: Get told by webhook or email when a firewall goes down or a certificate expires.

update.title: Updates
update.text: Set up the notice about new OPNexus versions and one-click updates.

done.backupBefore: You back up the OPNexus database on the server with
done.backupHelp: Covers the database (rules, hosts, history). API secrets and keys live in their own Docker volumes and are not in the dump. See the manual for details.
